name: Crisis Service Ribbon (miniature medal body)
size_basis: estimated: the body measured in the Vanguard product photograph against the suspension ribbon's width, 317 px taken as 0.6875 in (the miniature suspension ribbon, 11/16 in, CAPR 39-1 11.3 as compose.js MINI_DRAPE): body 0.7938 x 0.7959 in in the photograph. Height follows the body's own aspect. The width is the existing CAP asset's (0.625 in, assets/medals, kept as the brief asks; the photo measures 0.7938 in). The drawing keeps the width and the box; it is built from the photograph's own measured proportions (body width 367.4 px = 0.625 in).
ribbon_attach_note: ribbon_attach is the top centre of the suspension ring (or of the bail where the box cuts the ring away), on the body axis: the body is upright, the photograph's hang angle (1.1 deg) is removed; compose.js hangs it at the drape's V point

dimensions.ribbon_note: medal body only; the ribbon asset supplies the stripes and devices (ribbon_ref as the previous asset)

match_note: CAP body: the existing asset id and width of assets/medals/medal-crisis-ribbon-miniature; ribbon_ref as that asset

ribbon_ref.note: medal body only; the ribbon asset supplies the stripes and devices. ribbon_attach is the top of the suspension ring.

frame.note: body width 0.625 in (the spec width); every length below is inches in the medal frame (origin = body centre, +y down, upright)

gates.silhouette_iou: >= 0.95 (shipped upright miniature vs the photograph mask resampled into the same upright box)
gates.landmarks: every named feature centroid within 0.02 in of the reference
gates.edge_recall: lit-metal outline recall >= 0.80 within 0.012 in (0.006 in reported)
gates.ink_coverage: lit-metal area of mine / reference between 0.85 and 1.15 (body and named zones): letters and emblem strokes as solid as the reference
gates.ribbon_attach: top centre of the ring (or of the bail where the box cuts the ring) at the box top, x on the body axis

not_measurable: the field of the photograph is lit unevenly (darker toward the left edge and in a soft halo round the banner and the shield); the drawing uses one flat field tone and models the halo only as a dark recess round the banner, so the light-class gate is met by the seams, not by the lighting gradient

the photograph shows the pewter finish texture and the leaf veins as fine grain; each leaf is one pointed face with one recessed midrib (a straight line), not the two half-leaf planes of the engraving

the eagle device (0.22 in wide) is drawn from lib-b-eagle.js: a head in profile with a hooked beak turned left, a chest/neck body, two mirror-symmetric wings each of 5 primary blades, 6 secondary blades and 6 covert blades fanning from a shoulder point (blade tips, angles and lengths read off the 6500 px/in view: the scalloped lower edge shows about 11 feather tips per wing), two legs with 3 toes each, a lobed cloud behind the head (its 3 lobes are approximate) and a bar of 12 beads; the blade widths, the covert row and the toes are not separable in the photograph and are drawn at plausible sizes

the three words of the banner are read as CIVIL AIR on the left arm and PATROL on the right arm (the photograph prints no marks between them); the letter forms are the skeleton font, the engraved letters are slightly bolder and tilted
fidelity.note: Redrawn as clean parametric vector (LIVE13-ART 26, batch B): every element is modelled as the object it is (letters, stars, wreath leaves, banner, aircraft ...) with its proportions measured from the photograph and placed by measurement; flat tones with a lit and a shadow edge; upright. Replaces the traced body (LIVE13-ART 20).

fit_score.note: IoU of the shipped upright miniature against the photograph mask in the same box (lib-b.js)

notes: Designed miniature medal body (LIVE13-ART 26, batch B), upright. Measured from copy-of-life-saving.jpg (reference only, never shipped). Hang angle 1.1 deg of the photograph removed.
